europe_now.title: Spain Bans Evictions
europe_now.summary: Spain announced a nationwide ban on evictions following widespread public protests triggered by the eviction of an 87-year-old woman. The government has simultaneously introduced new housing measures to address the growing crisis.

sources.headline: Spain announces ban on evictions after protests over 87-year-old woman's eviction
Spain announces new housing measures after protests over 87-year-old woman's eviction

europe_now.title: Estonia Blames Russia for Arson Attack
europe_now.summary: Estonian authorities have officially blamed Russia for orchestrating an arson attack at a local defense company that supplies equipment to Ukraine. This incident highlights heightened security concerns and ongoing sabotage threats across the region.

sources.headline: Estonia blames Russia for arson at defence company supplying Ukraine

top_stories.title: EU Budget Negotiations and Funding Debates
top_stories.summary: Members of the European Parliament voted to approve significant new funds for the Erasmus program while frugal member states simultaneously push for broader budget reductions. Meanwhile, the European Union has moved to decrease funding for various internal programs, including women's rights organizations, as part of wider fiscal adjustments.

sources.headline: MEPs vote for €47bn in new Erasmus+ funds, as frugal states seek cuts to EU budget
EU reduces funds for women’s rights groups, in wider budget bonfire of good causes

top_stories.title: French Political Tensions and Far-Right Controversy
top_stories.summary: French far-right figures have launched legal action and accused opponents of waging a total war following severe antisemitism allegations directed at top party leadership. These political developments unfold alongside ongoing labor strikes and domestic unrest as civil servants demand increased budgetary resources.
